System: Equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (Nb: 16.67 at%, Mo: 16.67 at%, Ta: 16.67 at%, W: 16.67 at%, V: 16.67 at%, Ti: 16.67 at%) with oxygen introduction. Processing: Mechanical alloying of elemental powders (≥99.9% purity) in a high energy planetary ball mill with stainless steel balls/vial at a ball-to-powder weight ratio of 13:1 under high purity argon for 40 h; followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) of the 40 h milled powders in a graphite die at 1400 °C for 10 min under 30 MPa pressure, with a heating rate of 100 °C/min and cooling to 500 °C at 300 °C/min. Question: How can high-throughput computational screening be used to discover lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys with high-temperature strength superior to traditional ferritic superalloys?. System: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system (specifically Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 and Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5 as successful cases). Processing: Arc-melting of 99.9 wt% purity constituent elements, melted at least six times for homogeneity, followed by drop-casting; subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C and annealing at 700 °C for 2 hours for specific characterizations. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 700 °C) at a strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; in situ neutron scattering from room temperature to 1050 °C; synchrotron XRD and TEM characterization.
